answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to lock a bond before bidding for valuable jobs. After delivery, a randomly chosen auditor checks a verifiable result; if it fails the stated test, the bond is slashed, while honest agents recover it and earn fees. Creating a garden of fake identities cannot multiply influence for free: each one needs separate capital at risk. The ocean of possible pseudonyms still has to pass through this narrow jetty, and the attacker pays for every account they want to keep credible.
